proposed_destination.reason: Standing taste for character motion.

text: Jitter came from a 4 to 4.5 Hz damped wobble on nearly every beat (a swing every 3.3 frames): motion blur pulses at twice the wobble rate, 8 to 9 Hz, which is where human flicker sensitivity peaks. Per-part spins made it worse.

proposed_destination.reason: The cause behind the minimum half-period gate; kept as the explanation builders need.

text: Sub-frame staggers (35 ms and 55 ms are 1.05 and 1.65 frames) mean no two parts ever sit at the same phase of a frame or shutter, so every part's blur looks different. Offsets between parts must be whole frames.

proposed_destination.reason: Explains the whole-frame offset rule the symmetry gate enforces.

text: A strong out-ease leaves rest at 6.25 times its average speed and covers 34% of a 16-frame move in its first frame, so the blur jumps from none to a long streak in one frame; an exit ease that ends at 1.66 times average speed does the same at the end.

proposed_destination.reason: Why rig parts use zero-velocity-end curves; the acceleration gate catches it.

text: Parts were cut off at container edges because nothing checked the character's envelope against clipping containers, and a colour mixed by distance from the disc flickered at the disc's edge.

proposed_destination.reason: The cause behind the clipping gate and colour-by-progress rule.

text: A mark whose parts overlap by design shows seams and double shadows when each part is drawn separately with its own opacity, paper edge and shadow; parts in preserve-3d at the same depth z-fight; and a spread that hovers near the split point flickers between fused and split.

proposed_destination.reason: The causes behind the sheet, 2D-only and split-point rules.

text: Model a multi-part mark as one part replicated N times: any motion defined once for part 0, then copied with a rotation and a whole-frame delay, stays symmetric by construction.

proposed_destination.reason: The plan's motif rig generalized from the films' character (N-part marks).

text: Compute a fused mark's geometry facts from its SVG before animating it: where it splits apart when all parts spread in unison, where one group alone splits it, where same-group parts first touch pulling in, and where the centre hole closes.

proposed_destination.target: engine/remotion/kit/motif/ (geometry analysis from the brand SVG)
proposed_destination.reason: The rig needs these thresholds; the specific numbers belong to the brand's mark.

text: The films' mark geometry (eight rounded squares on a ring, split at +0.248 ring radii, sizes per disc diameter) is one brand's data.

proposed_destination.reason: Brand-specific geometry; it lives in the private pack, never in the core.

text: A motif rig has a closed set of channels: whole-mark turn (rests at multiples of the symmetry angle), whole-avatar scale, mark scale inside its disc, mark offset, and per part only radial offset, scale and an away position. Nothing else moves: no per-part angle, no per-part spin.

proposed_destination.reason: A closed channel set is what makes symmetry and gating possible.

text: Every kit component's pose is a pure function of the film frame, including the renderer's sub-frame samples: nothing carried between frames, no per-part timers, no randomness or noise, nothing cached.

proposed_destination.reason: The one-clock law applied to every component.

text: Any frame rendered on its own is bit-identical to the same frame rendered in sequence.

proposed_destination.reason: Acceptance test 1; measurable by rendering sampled frames alone and in sequence and hashing.

text: Every key sits on a whole frame and every per-part offset is a whole number of frames, so part k at frame f is exactly part 0 at frame f minus its offset, rotated, blur samples included; blur streaks become rotated copies of one another, not per-part noise.

proposed_destination.reason: The rig only accepts integer frame offsets.

text: Clean multi-part loaders all phase-lock by position: SpinKit's circle delays each of 12 dots by cycle / 12, iOS's replicator uses duration / count, After Effects' follow-the-leader rig is valueAtTime(time - index x delay); biology calls it a metachronal rhythm and perception calls it common fate.

proposed_destination.reason: The research behind the rig, kept with its sources.

text: A multi-part mark uses only three phase relationships: unison (offset 0), pairs (one group lagged by a fixed whole-frame lag), and wave (each slot offset by step x k, where the step is the cycle / part count). No other staggers.

proposed_destination.reason: The rig exposes exactly these modes; the symmetry gate verifies them.

text: Derive a motif's lags from the product's own loader timing (in the films, the loader ran one group 8% of a cycle behind, which became a 4-frame lag on a 48-frame breath).

proposed_destination.reason: Onboarding method; the values are brand data.

text: A wave's step is its cycle divided by the part count, in whole frames, and at least 2 frames so each accent registers (animators hold an accent at least two frames; the films used 3).

proposed_destination.reason: A rig constraint with a sourced minimum.

text: Order parts by slot (where they are now, counted clockwise from twelve o'clock), not by part identity, because every turn moves each part one slot along.

proposed_destination.reason: A rig implementation rule.

text: Spoke and orientation lock: every part's centre stays on its spoke at the mark's turn plus its slot angle, only its distance changes, and its own turn is always its rest turn plus the mark's turn. Unison keeps all parts identical under rotation at every frame, pairs keep each group identical, and wave keeps slot k at frame f equal to slot 0 at f minus step x k.

proposed_destination.reason: The plan's symmetry gate for mark rigs, checked on the motion trace at every sub-sample.

text: Gestures that break the ring do so on purpose (a part sent to a target, a gather): the parts left on the ring stay exactly at rest. An entrance may spiral each group in as one rigid piece.

proposed_destination.reason: Declared exceptions the symmetry gate must know about.

text: Good radial marks change the whole mark at once: an assistant ring that moves outward when responding and inward when listening, dots rooted in consistent paths and timing, a breathing flower driven by one container animation with no per-part delay.

proposed_destination.reason: Reference research for motif design.

text: Minimum half-period of 8 frames: any channel's consecutive direction reversals are at least 8 frames apart, so a full swing takes at least 16 frames (1.9 Hz or slower at 29.97 fps). No flutter or wobble faster than that anywhere.

proposed_destination.reason: The plan's no-loop-faster-than-16-frames gate.

text: At most one overshoot per gesture, and a character's whole vocabulary gets one overshoot at most, approved by the requester for that character only.

proposed_destination.reason: Measurable on the trace; the allowlist records the approved gesture.

text: Nothing loops except an explicit thinking state, whose cycle is at least 44 frames. No idle loops.

proposed_destination.reason: Loops carry loop_period in the motion trace; anything shorter or undeclared fails.

text: Blur length follows speed, so a wobble at f Hz makes the blur pulse at 2f; flicker sensitivity peaks near 8 Hz. Keep oscillation well below 4 Hz.

proposed_destination.reason: The physics behind the period gate.

text: Springs in good motion systems settle rather than bounce: Material 3 fires even its bounciest spring once per transition and its effects springs never overshoot; Apple defaults to bounce 0, calls about 0.3 noticeable and above about 0.4 exaggerated for UI, and starts every spring at 100% damping.

proposed_destination.reason: Sourced reference values for spring policy.

text: Add motion purposefully, aim for brevity and precision, and avoid objects that oscillate in a sustained way (Apple HIG).

proposed_destination.reason: A sourced principle for the motion skill.

text: Stacked out-of-phase loops read as swimming.

proposed_destination.reason: A glitch pattern builders should recognize.

text: Zero velocity at both ends: every rig move starts and ends at rest, or hands its exact velocity to the next move. Rig parts never use strong out-eases, exits, snaps or linear; only the rig's rest-to-rest curves.

proposed_destination.reason: Measurable on rig traces: velocity at segment ends.

text: Peak speed is at most 30 px per frame for every point at 1920x1080: with 16 samples over a 180 degree shutter the gap between samples is speed / 32, so 30 px per frame keeps it under 1 px. Up to 48 px per frame only at the crest of a flight longer than 570 px when the beat can't afford a slower one.

proposed_destination.reason: The plan's speed gate, scaled to the film's height.

text: Acceleration is at most 8 px per frame squared: a point's per-frame movement changes by no more than 8 px between frames, so its blur length changes by no more than 4 px. A strong out-ease breaks this on its first frame for any move longer than about 24 px.

proposed_destination.reason: The plan's acceleration gate.

text: Strobing is too much visual change between adjacent frames, not a frame-rate problem; ease curves jerk to a halt where springs keep their velocity; After Effects' old 16-sample blur cap produced visible echoes on fast objects.

proposed_destination.reason: Sourced reasons behind the speed and acceleration limits.

text: Model every gesture numerically at the smallest, typical and largest size it appears before building it, and record the worst case.

proposed_destination.reason: A design-time check; the gates re-check the rendered trace.

proposed_destination.reason: Structural default that prevents clipping.

proposed_destination.reason: Acceptance test 7; measurable from layout boxes and the rig envelope.

text: Inside a scroll view, a character crosses the view's edge only when it's calm.

proposed_destination.reason: Staging rule for builders.

text: Opacity goes on the whole mark or a whole sheet, never on a single part while parts touch.

proposed_destination.reason: Rig render rule that prevents seams.

proposed_destination.reason: Rig render rule that prevents double shadows.
